Hypercasual Teardown

Flip Trickster

The hard part is deciding when to stop flipping.

Hold to prepare, release to jump, tuck to rotate, then open the body before contact. More rotation promises more score; a late release can turn ambition into a crash.

Precision + expressive objectivesSingle jumps + six-jump toursMobile web adaptation brief
The gestureJudging a jumpTours & progressionEconomyProduct contextBuild layerSources

01 · The gesture

One touch has four meanings

The input is small; the state model is not. The same held finger prepares a jump on the ground and changes rotation in the air.

ReadHeight, target, surface and current objective.
PrepareHold; the body crouches and leans.
CommitRelease; the launch becomes a trajectory.
ShapeHold in flight to tuck, release to extend.
ResolveContact, score, goal state; retry or continue.

The tutorial makes a held touch bodily before it makes it numerical. The crouch gives anticipation and the release has an obvious consequence. Independent play adds the real question: how much flight can be spent rotating before the body must be opened for landing? A stance control offers another orientation, while later objectives alter what counts as a desirable jump.

Flight is a shared budget

Stay tuckedAccumulate rotations.
Spend the remaining alignment window.
⇄
Extend earlierMake foot orientation easier to read.
Give up another possible revolution.

A qualitative decision model, not a measured physics equation. Launch travel and aerial orientation remain distinct problems.

The angle of the landing surface matters as well as the angle of the body. A flat gym mat, a narrow wooden dock and a crater slope can require different release decisions even with the same number of flips. Height changes available flight; target placement changes travel; an authored constraint changes which solution is worth attempting.

02 · Judgment

A record and a task are different achievements

The result has several axes: current score, persistent best, score thresholds and a behavioral objective. A single green check cannot explain all four.

Precision multiplies an accumulated score

One inspected dock landing moves from 308 to 462 with ×1.5 displayed. Other jumps show ×1.2 and ×2.0. These states establish landing bonuses; they do not reveal a universal height formula or prove an exact mapping from every colored ring to every multiplier.

A later retry can score less than the existing best while leaving old checkmarks intact. That is useful persistence, but it can make a mediocre attempt look as though it completed every goal. The target should label “This jump” and “Best” separately.

The strongest level variation changes the desired behavior rather than merely raising a number. “Crash land” rewards a controlled failure shape. “Wait one second before tucking” asks the player to withhold the most obvious aerial action. “Land past the target” makes overshooting purposeful. These are independent predicates on a jump, not decorative names for high scores.

Failure teaches only when its cause remains visible. The dock attempt falls beside the target; retry restores the same spatial problem without a coin deduction in the checked interval. That creates a useful learning loop: change one preparation or release decision, then compare the next contact. Persistent goals reward accumulated mastery while immediate feedback must explain the latest attempt.

Preserve the reason to correct the next jump. A generic “failed” banner is weaker than showing which surface or body contact caused the outcome.

03 · Progression

Practice one jump. Then perform the whole tour.

Individual levels isolate problems; Full Stage tests a sequence of them. It is an aggregate performance, not a sudden-death run.

The Island tour carries 369 points into its second jump. That jump crashes, its contribution is discarded, and the next platform starts with the same 369. Later successful jumps raise the total; another crash again leaves it unchanged. The final total is 4037. This matters to the player's commitment: a mistake damages the score but leaves the remaining tour worth playing.

Access, mastery and variety reinforce one another

The early Gym explicitly asks for its silver score goal to unlock the next level. Higher scores and special objectives supply replay targets. Full Stage then turns familiar platforms into a new score context; it also adds goals such as a quad flip or landing outside targets across a tour.

Changing the diorama gives the player a new visual promise, but the meaningful variation comes from the platform, landing surface, flight space and objective. The same touch vocabulary survives that escalation.

The source recordings expose different catalogues: the early route reaches The Park; the later carousel shows nine playable themes and a separate Tutorial. They do not establish one version's exhaustive level list. The complete target deliberately combines those themes; its scope is defined in the Build layer.

04 · Economy

Coins buy identity or bypass, not a stronger body

The source uses earned rewards as both mastery confirmation and a route around a difficult level. Cosmetic purchases are a separate expression of progress.

The checked purchase spends 90 of 100 coins and loads the next setup at 10. The three-skip bundle costs 180, less per skip than the single. This gives accumulated rewards a practical use when the current goal resists mastery. It also creates a design tension: a bypass can protect continuation, but should not claim the player performed an objective they skipped.

Reward the milestone once

The inspected threshold reward moves 1135 to 1150 while showing +15. Other recorded balances and offers demonstrate an earned coin economy, but do not fully reveal its payout schedule or anti-repeat rules. The adaptation therefore needs an explicit grant ledger rather than assuming every retry pays.

The headwear preview supplies a harmless long-term choice. Its desired function is visible identity, with the body's contact silhouette and collision rules preserved. The target should keep a complete earnable cosmetic set before considering optional platform Extras.

05 · Product context

Easy access, demanding correction

The appeal is immediate bodily comedy and a precision skill ceiling. The demanded player tolerates repeated attempts and learns to distinguish a useful crash from a bad landing.

The current US iOS listing is free with in-app purchases; its seller is 7 Minute Games Corporation and its copyright names Lion Studios. It supports iPhone and iPad. These current storefront identities should not be projected onto the unknown versions in the recordings. App Store, checked 5 October 2026.

Development & Production

The iOS history shows repeated generic fix notes through 2024–2025 and currently labels version 1.11.67 “Feb 9,” without a year in the retrieved label. Those notes do not identify a collision fix. The recordings show contact anomalies; whether a current build still has them is unverified. That makes reproducible contact classification and finite crash recovery better regression targets than an attempt to preserve old glitches. Version history.

A displayed player review dated 28 February 2018 criticizes jump power while enjoying landings and falls. It is a dated individual opinion, not a measured complaint rate. The corresponding target test is concrete: preparation must visibly explain travel and repeated identical inputs must produce consistent outcomes. No documented engine, team size, budget, acquisition cost or revenue was established. Attributed player review.

Source monetization and target friction

The recordings contain banners, an interstitial, double-coin/free-prize offers and Remove Ads/Restore controls. Their trigger schedule, ad provider and current prices are not established. Advertising after all worlds are cleared is a narrator assertion, not a general rule proved by these states.

For bug.games, the complete play loop stays available offline. Optional Extras are distinct additions; they do not sell recovery from an unexplained landing. There is no assumed ad API, coin top-up or creator payout model.

The adaptation should keep precision, ridiculous outcomes and a visible correction while improving result clarity and recovery.

Complete target scope · Designed

The free base is a finite stunt tour followed by voluntary mastery replay. It contains one embedded training sequence, ten locations with six authored single-jump levels each, and a six-jump Full Stage tour per location. All sixty levels, all ten tours, both stances, all behavioral families, local coin progression, the earnable cosmetic catalogue, skips, save/continue and Settings are required in this build. The final Space tour closes the route with a results ceremony and returns to replay; this is a Designed conclusion, not a claim about the source ending.

Campaign content grammar: Gym teaches launch, landing and objective separation; Park adds surfaces and intentional overshoot; Mountain increases drop and slope; City uses roof gaps and narrow safe platforms; Funhouse mixes platform heights and deceptive but readable target sizes; Factory uses beams and elevated obstacles; Ship uses decks, masts and narrow planks; Island uses cliffs, dock and boat landings; Haunted House uses roof edges and branching landing surfaces; Space combines tall drops, antenna contact and steep terrain. Each six-jump set must include an approachable entry, a precision change, an objective change, a higher-flight problem, a geometry challenge and a culmination. This is a Designed curriculum grounded in shown themes; unseen source layouts are creative design space. Moving hazards are not required source mechanics.

Principles: create situations by changing height, reach, surface and desired behavior; teach one change before combining it; reward a readable correction and persistent mastery; preserve a useful tour after a crash. Larger scores must come from meaningful execution, not from buying a stronger body. A successful special crash is distinguishable from an ordinary missed landing.

Core statements

  1. C1: The player reads launch and landing geometry, prepares with hold and commits with release; different preparation changes the travel problem.
  2. C2: During flight, tuck versus extension changes rotation; seeking another revolution competes with timely body alignment. Success must not be automatic.
  3. C3: The same jump can achieve score progress without satisfying its behavioral objective. Persistent best/flags never masquerade as this attempt’s accomplishment.
  4. C4: Full Stage keeps an aggregate total across six one-attempt jumps; an ordinary crash contributes zero and the remaining tour still matters.
  5. C5: Failure → same-layout retry permits a changed preparation/release decision; there is no mandatory purchase, ad or stamina cost to retry.

Mobile loop and input · Designed

Entry opens on the safe training ledge or last unlocked selection without a long splash. First touch begins preparation; release commits; airborne hold/release shapes rotation; contact resolves; result offers Retry or Continue. Individual jumps target roughly 3–8 seconds of active flight and preparation after familiarity, with unconstrained inspection time; these are target tuning intentions, not source measurements. A six-jump tour aims for a short repeatable visit, but progress checkpoints survive longer sessions. Difficulty grows through reach, surface, height and objective combinations rather than input latency or a larger touch vocabulary.

Action / contextOutcomeCancellation and interruption
Idle play pad: hold then releaseCrouch/lean visibly; release launches using the tuned preparation state. A quick tap is a short preparation, never a menu selection.Pointer leaving pad while held remains captured; pointercancel/visibility loss cancels preparation without launching. Ignore second simultaneous pointer.
Airborne play pad: hold/releaseTuck/increase rotation; release extends/reduces rotation, never teleports or snaps automatically upright.No rewind mid-flight. Lost touch/pointercancel pauses into a neutral overlay, clears held state and resumes with a fresh gesture without queued input.
Stance/Map/Settings/RetrySeparate 44 px-or-larger targets; stance only while idle. Map selection inspects before Play commits.Panel taps never reach play pad. Retry current jump; tour restart explicitly labelled and confirms scope. Coin Buy/Skip have distinct preview and confirm.
Focus loss, host pause, rotationPause simulation and active gameplay accounting; clear pending gesture, preserve state, mute as required.Resume overlay accepts fresh input. Landscape letterboxes/reframes without changing simulation or score; no required orientation lock/fullscreen/vibration.
Settings during playSwitch whole interface EN/RU; separate music/effects sliders 0–100%; preferences save locally.Returning does not launch or tuck. No long settings screen before first play; storage denial gives temporary preferences without breaking play.

Use one hand in a 390×844 portrait browser/iframe. Keep the lower play pad within thumb reach; reserve the scene above it for launch, entire target and body orientation. HUD, floating score and celebratory effects must not cover the contact at the decision moment. Inspecting a goal or cosmetic must work without hover. Meaningful visual feedback must remain comprehensible with both audio channels muted.

Art and signal direction · Designed

Build an original geometric stunt playground: faceted athlete, crisp body poses, tactile foam/wood/rock surfaces and bright square target layers. Keep the source’s readable flight silhouette and warm, comic consequence; improve material separation and portrait framing. A consistent side-oblique camera must show takeoff, landing surface and entire flight, with thumb controls below the scene and a small goal/score rail above. Crouch gives anticipation, launch creates commitment, contact gets one readable impact beat, and crash/success recovers to a clearly available action. Do not build a Roblox skin or use the source’s models, logos, streamer overlays or evidence frames as game assets.

Reduced motion/effects option may reduce embellishment without deleting information.
Fonts/UICompact geometric display +high-legibility body, all locale states fit; whole player interface EN/RU.System/embedded OFL fonts or original UI; no external requests.44 px touch targets, fit Cyrillic, contrast check and no clipped tutorial text.
Checked donor figures for the two pilot transfers

Secondary analytical references only. P1 is checked placement→different outcome in a different physics puzzle; transfer is the visible cause and same-problem retry. P2 is checked result hierarchy in a tactics game; transfer is clear advancement versus optional mastery. Neither proves retention gains or supplies reusable assets.

Audio and motion event sheet · Designed

Original audio fidelity is unverified: downloaded clips contain audio, but this authoring session did not hear them through an audio-capable analysis tool. Reported whooshes, flip chimes, impact cracks and fanfare are unverified source descriptions. The following is a complete production brief for target assets, not certification of those descriptions.

TriggerPurpose / desired soundMotion/readiness / mixAsset status
Hold → crouchQuiet elastic cloth/air anticipation, with subtle rising tension; do not reward holding forever.Track preparation without masking the release; no requirement to infer pose through sound.New original/licensed cue needed; deliberate procedural approximation allowed if listened to and expressive.
Release → launchShort airy release and foot push, with a clear attack.Starts on commitment, not menu touch; voice/goal messages take precedence.New short SFX; no original ripped audio.
Completed revolutionDistinct compact rising note; later revolutions vary pitch within a bounded pleasant range.Exactly once per milestone; avoid piled-up chimes during rapid spins. Visual label carries same meaning.Original synthesized/recorded or licensed SFX, checked by listening.
Clean contact /precision settleSoft material thud plus brief bright precision cue, strength coherent with ring tier.Contact compression precedes settled score; duck background music briefly. No fanfare before outcome classification.Coherent foam/wood/rock cue family, ready assets preferred when texture matters; licence per file.
Ordinary crash /authored crash goalComic low thump and light rattle; avoid graphic injury. Special objective adds a distinct success cue after contact.Finite ragdoll recovery; Retry becomes usable immediately at stable result. Crash noise never drowns cause text.Original/licensed event sounds and variation; not a source bone-snap recreation.
New goal, coins, cosmetic equip, tour finishSmall milestone chord, short coin confirmation, equip tick; richer tour cadence only on final settle.Exactly once per ledger grant/equip; replayed old goal gets no reward sound.New event assets, normalized gain and repeat testing.
Practice and ordinary jumps: musicSparse playful marimba/plucked-percussion loop with warm bass and air; leave flight cues room.Moderate pulse selected by listening; no measured source BPM. Seamless loop, low-density during decisions, quieter in menus.Original music-capable generation or permissively licensed finished track; final audio embedded.
Full Stage/final result: musicSame instrumental family, a slightly firmer pulse across the tour, and a short resolved ending.No abrupt restart after every platform; pause, resume and mute preserve appropriate phrase/input state.Original/ready licensed loop plus cadence; no source fidelity claim.

Music and effects use independent gain buses. Sliders are touch-usable 0–100% with visible value and mute state; changing one cannot change the other. Start/resume audio only after a gesture. Platform mute silences both without overwriting chosen slider values. Save EN/RU and both levels as device preferences separate from monotonic progress. Translate onboarding, HUD, results, goal names, errors, save notices, preview and unavailable-offer text. For example Settings/Настройки, Music/Музыка, Sound effects/Звуковые эффекты, This jump/Этот прыжок, Retry/Повторить are target interface strings, not an authored translation of this report.

Asset production contract: for each important character/environment/UI/effect/SFX/music family, choose ready licensed work, original generated work or deliberate code construction because it fits the style. Verify each actual file’s author/licence/format and commercial-use/modification rights; prefer CC0, MIT, Apache or OFL as appropriate, skip unclear/ripped/NC/ND material. Download the real file rather than a preview, integrate and inspect/listen in play. Keep ASSETS.md internally and embed required licence credits in the delivered game HTML. Placeholders are not a final quality target; name blocked assets if sourcing fails. Use consistent proportions, palette, filtering, light and sound loudness.

Roblox analogs and the first 20 minutes · Designed

Bloom Brain’s bundled locator found 619 local pages and ran lexical search with --no-semantic. Queries: obby failure retry checkpoint readable landing feedback; first action contextual instruction prompt feedback obby. Selected pages were read locally; referenced donor image files were not found, so this is checked secondary text, not a newly observed Roblox playthrough. No Roblox usage figures or retention claims are imported.

ProblemChecked analog / provenanceTransfer / risk / test
H1 · First action changes meaning by stateSteal a Chicken, artifacts/pages/steal-a-chicken.md, snapshot 2026-09-08, §3 First contact / §6 System composition. EV005/006/008 locators describe failure feedback then Go to Pen/placement.Use state-driven “Hold to prepare”→“Release to jump”→“Hold to tuck”→“Release to land”, then fade prompts after demonstrated independent use. Carry only contextual next-action instruction, no theft, production, stat economy or multiplayer. Hypothesis: first independent two-touch jump becomes explainable; test player identifies action in each state without auto-solution. Risk: prompts obscure body or prescribe exact release moment.
Failure should invite a correctionTower of Hell, artifacts/pages/tower-of-hell-technical-teardown.md, snapshot 2026-09-05, §04 no checkpoints. Reported fall→whole-climb replay produces explicit frustration.Reject whole-tour reset, paid checkpoints and shared timer. This is a negative reference for C4/C5, not an accepted positive mechanism or a retention comparison.
Surface-similar backflips should not replace precisionBackflip Obby Escape, artifacts/pages/backflip-obby-escape-teardown.md, snapshot 2026-08-07, §04/§21. Spam jump grows Total Speed and upgrades.Reject spam-to-stat progression, rebirth and multipliers: they would change the reason for a touch. Keep this game’s body orientation decision.
CheckpointIntended ordinary play / feedbackNext pull
~30 secondsTry the safe ledge, see hold→crouch→release and one contact; a failure has a visible cause.Correct one gesture; no store or offer.
~2 minutesPerform independent tuck/release, compare This jump with Best; recognize a new score goal.Try a higher tier or the next unlocked geometry.
~5 minutesMeet an objective that changes behavior, such as delayed tuck or deliberate crash.One familiar input produces a new solution; earned badge/coins confirms it.
~10 minutesAttempt a six-jump tour; a crash damages its score without ending it.Finish remaining platforms, then retry a weak individual setup.
~20 minutesChoose new theme or revisit optional mastery; cosmetic equip is player-initiated after learning.An unfinished personal target and geometric variety, saved for return. No guaranteed completion time or invented retention uplift.

These are experience checkpoints, not timed reward quotas. Check them through normal one-handed phone play; a technique only becomes accepted production behavior after it is implemented and played. Do not insert quests, dailies, server systems or economic rewards merely to fill a checkpoint.

bug.games plan · complete free base, optional Extras

This is a publication and implementation plan. No game has been built, submitted or published in this session. The live SDK documentation was retrieved on 5 October 2026. The base game must remain playable as a single offline HTML with embedded art, fonts and sound; platform integration is a guarded adapter when served on bug.games. Do not load the platform SDK for a local file or an unrelated host. On the platform, attempt the documented /sdk/bloomplay.js integration; if it is absent or initialization fails, retain local play and honest unavailable states without inventing a successful platform connection.

ConcernImplementation contractVerification
State and SDK lifecycleInitialize once; use gameplayStart/gameplayStop only for actual active-play transitions. Stop on result, map, settings, focus loss or host pause. Resume after an explicit action. onPause clears held touch and pauses physics; onMute silences both buses without replacing preferences.No duplicate starts/stops; a host pause cannot launch on return. Native events and custom analytics must not double count the same transition.
Progress and settingsVersioned, guarded local storage works without a platform. Optional SDK save keeps progression separate from device preferences: merge best=max, goals/owned/grants=OR and unlocked reach=max; never combine coin balances by max or sum blindly. Reconcile an idempotent grant/spend ledger with a known revision before changing balances.Failed cloud read is unknown, not an empty account. Do not overwrite a known remote save after a transient failure. Reload cannot repeat grants or spends. Unsupported storage gives playable temporary progress plus a concise notice.
Native milestonesDeclare exact milestone names in the draft metadata. Call progress.moment(name) only at their meaningful first completion, with a persisted dedupe flag; inspect current SDK behavior at implementation.Do not fire from merely opening a map, equipping a preview or importing a save. Check an ordinary route and reload, plus SDK-absent behavior.
Optional productsLaunch metadata has products:[] because no platform Extra exists. The earned headwear and skips use only local game coins. A proposed Sunset Style Pack would add three original cosmetic appearances beyond the twelve free options, with unchanged physics. It is planned/unbuilt and has no live price, Buy button or entitlement now.Do not promote an idea as a working shop. The full base is complete before optional Extra work. No sold progression, retry, stat boost, top-up or ad income is assumed.
If an Extra is later builtFinish and play its actual assets, previews, entitlement and restore path. Use SDK getProducts() and current returned sellable catalogue, price and currency; never cache a fake price. A successful empty response means no available products, without asserting an approval reason. Confirmed ownership takes precedence over catalogue availability.Insufficient balance, failure or cancelled purchase grants nothing. A successful durable purchase grants only confirmed entitlement; restore/reload survives. Clear held input across purchase overlay; resume audio/play only appropriately. Explain unavailable state without guessing pending-review status.
Store presentationUse a truthful hook, short visit estimate, one player, touch/mouse controls and playable screenshots from the actual adaptation. The report’s evidence images are analytical references, not store or game artwork.Credits and licences verified per file; eventual original title/branding and publisher approval require review. No recommendation to publish copied models, logos, videos or source audio.

Analytics questions: can a new player understand the two meanings of hold; identify a failed contact; correct it; distinguish access from optional mastery; and continue a tour after a crash? Record enough event context to answer these without sending raw gesture streams or personal identifiers. Never present design hypotheses as measured retention improvements.

Custom event / native momentWhen / minimal propertiesDecision it supports
first_action_completed / “First jump”First actual launch release; tutorial stage and elapsed-to-action bucket. Fire once per new local profile.First-action completion divided by valid new entries; compare elapsed distributions, excluding preloaded accounts.
jump_resolvedExactly once after contact settles; stage_id, mode, stance, flip_count, contact_zone, outcome, score and new_goal_ids. Define enumerations; avoid device/user identifiers.Per-stage attempts and contact causes. Diagnose a narrow orientation window versus a confusing landing surface.
retry_selectedAfter resolved jump, before restoring same setup; stage_id, outcome and attempt number.Retry per resolved failure; meaningful correction judged through local play plus outcome/stance changes, not raw repeated clicks.
goal_earned / “First silver” / “First special goal”Only new goal flag; stage_id, goal_id, kind, attempt number. Native milestone first completion only.Access milestone versus optional skill. Goal completion divided by players/attempts who encountered that authored goal.
tour_resolved / “First Full Stage”After sixth jump; location_id, total, crash_count, new_goal_ids.Tour completion among starts, and continuation after a nonterminal crash; distinguish voluntary exit from pause.
location_unlocked / “New location” / “Space unlocked”First valid unlock; location_id and earned/bypassed access.Understand route progression without claiming a skipped badge was earned.
skip_committed / cosmetic_committed / “First earned cosmetic”Only successful local spend; item_id, local_coin_cost and balance_after. Preview/cancel is separate only if needed for a real question.Earned resource utility and whether bypass clusters on an unclear problem. Never conflate these local coins with platform purchase revenue.
campaign_completed / “Tour complete”All intended access route and final Space tour finished; route version and bypass count.Completion among valid starts plus return to optional mastery. Time/session estimates stay hypotheses until measured.

Native page/session/lifecycle measurements belong to the SDK; custom events above add game meaning. Establish event definitions and denominators before examining a cohort, test idempotency after reload/pause, then compare stage and objective cohorts. Small samples and edited source footage cannot justify uplift claims. If the SDK is unavailable, the game continues; do not silently claim successful telemetry delivery.

Acceptance cases for the future game

These are required scenarios for implementation review, not tests run on a game in this authoring session. Freeze the route and objective inventory before building; package validation of this report proves neither tuned physics nor campaign completeness. Test ordinary play without debug unlocks, plus targeted interruption and transaction cases.

Case / coreStarting state and actionRequired outcome / evidence to retain
AC1 · C1, H1Fresh profile at the safe ledge; hold, release, then independently use airborne hold/release.Visible preparation and committed launch; state-specific prompt changes and fades after competence. First meaningful action happens in the play scene, with no store detour. Retain phone play observation.
AC2 · C1–C2Same authored layout and stance; repeat identical inputs, then change preparation or tuck release. Try early/late release and both stances.Stable inputs give consistent travel/contact; changed input can correct overrotation or reach. No automatic upright snap, hidden success roll or costume collision advantage. Retain actual sequences and tuned parameters; source numbers are not calibration.
AC3 · C5, P1Miss the dock beside the target; inspect the settled result and select Retry.The contact cause remains readable, Retry is already available, same layout restores without cost. Player can name one correction; no purchase/ad/full campaign reset. Check cause cue does not cover the body on phone.
AC4 · C3, P2Saved Best above 600 with old flags; make a current jump below 300.This jump and Best are labelled separately; old badges stay earned without claiming this attempt completed them. Access status and optional goals form a readable hierarchy; Continue is not obscured.
AC5 · C3A delayed-tuck goal with a score goal unmet; a purposeful crash on the named surface; a clean landing past target.Each behavior is judged by its own explicit predicate, not by score alone. A special crash can earn its objective while an ordinary crash scores zero. Exact target predicates/boundaries documented; no undeserved old/new check swap.
AC6 · C4Full Stage total 369 before the second jump; crash; complete remaining platforms including another failure.Second jump contributes 0, third begins 369; all six get one attempt, final total sums only settled contributions. Distinct tour-best/goals. Verify tour restart label and nonterminal crash through normal play.
AC7 · Local resource ledger100 coins; confirm one 90-coin skip, cancel an unaffordable purchase, then try a three-token bundle with enough funds. Reload near commit.Single skip leaves 10 and marks access Bypassed, not earned mastery. Bundle grants three tokens and keeps unused ones. Cancel/failure changes nothing; no duplicate grant/spend on reload; actual reward budget supports the earnable catalog.
AC8 · Contact and recoveryHigh flight, narrow edge, steep slope, flat-body contact and repeated rapid rotations.No tunneling, stretched body, NaN, endless ragdoll or unstoppable jump. Consistent named contact classification, finite recovery and visible Retry. Target does not preserve the anomalous back-landing loophole.
AC9 · Whole campaignFresh ordinary-play route through training, 60 authored jumps and 10 tours; use every objective family and finish Space.No repeated placeholder layout, missing scene, dead unlock or unattainable mandatory threshold. Ending returns to replay. Record coverage matrix, ordinary route, longest correction loop, coin earning/spending and real play duration.
AC10 · PersistenceReload at a new goal grant, coin spend, tour transition and selection. Deny storage; simulate cloud read failure.Monotonic records survive supported save paths; ledger stays consistent; preferences stay separate. Denied storage preserves play with a notice. Unknown remote read does not overwrite cloud progress.
AC11 · Platform lifecycleRun standalone offline; absent SDK; initialization failure; platform-ready mode; host pause/mute and focus loss during a hold.Base remains playable. Starts/stops/moments are not duplicated. Return clears held input and never commits launch. Mute respects saved sliders. Live telemetry only claimed after successful adapter verification.
AC12 · Language/audioSwitch EN/RU in settings mid-session; music 0/effects 80, then music 60/effects 0; pause, reload and host mute/unmute.Whole UI remains legible and translated, both sliders independent and remembered. Audio unlock uses a gesture; no sound at first load without permission, no burst of queued effects on resume. Listen to the final real assets.
AC13 · Mobile flowOne-handed 390×844 portrait iframe/browser, also landscape and desktop. Test flight, results, map, shop, settings, 20-minute visit.Thumb/HUD never cover decisive contact.44 px targets, no hover requirements, panels consume taps, pointercancel has safe behavior. Check actual phone performance; emulation alone cannot establish battery/audio/browser support.
AC14 · Art, audio and packagingOpen delivered game HTML offline; play every theme, wear each hat, listen to every event/music context.All required assets present and coherent, with per-file commercial licence evidence/credits. No evidence screenshot or ripped asset in game. Name unavailable final assets; do not conceal placeholders or claim untested visual/audio quality.
AC15 · Optional Extra only if subsequently builtFinished pack plus test catalog success/empty/error, confirmed owned item unavailable for sale, insufficient balance, cancel/success/restore.Preview is reversible; only confirmed entitlement unlocks. Current sellable catalogue controls purchase/price. Existing ownership survives catalogue change. Planned content has no Buy. Input and both audio buses restore safely.

Specification readiness: ready with named limits. The complete target and its acceptance route are defined; unresolved source coefficients, original audio, exact source catalogue/version, fine objective boundaries and end-state are declared design space or fidelity limits. Physics tuning, production assets, phone performance, SDK execution and actual full-campaign play are work for the game build, not accomplishments of this report.
